mechanism_narrative: Continued recovery in WORKPLACES mobility, improving from -60.9 to -42.0 over the past four weeks, signals renewed commuting and daytime activity that spills over into retail footfall, pushing RETAIL_REC higher over the next four weeks.
evidence_refs: fact:WORKPLACES improved by 18.9 points over the last four weeks
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC fails to increase (mean next 28 days <= mean last 28 days) despite WORKPLACES continuing to rise over the next four weeks.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained decline in RESIDENTIAL mobility below 30 percent-above-baseline indicates people spending less time at home, which historically coincides with increased discretionary outings and retail/recreation visits in the following two weeks.
candidate_trigger: RESIDENTIAL falls below 30.0 percent-above-baseline on a weekly mean
evidence_refs: fact:RESIDENTIAL declined from 39.4 to 32.1 over the last four weeks
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC does not rise in the two weeks following a week where RESIDENTIAL mean drops below 30, or RESIDENTIAL stalls above 30 while RETAIL_REC still rises.

mechanism_narrative: In an active easing-of-restrictions policy regime, continued increases in TRANSIT usage, rising from -64.6 to -53.9, indicate loosened mobility policy that permits greater movement to retail and recreation venues, driving RETAIL_REC upward over the next four weeks.
evidence_refs: fact:TRANSIT mobility improved for three consecutive weeks reaching -53.9
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC fails to increase despite TRANSIT continuing to rise during an active easing regime, or policy tightens causing TRANSIT to reverse without RETAIL_REC following.

mechanism_narrative: Simultaneous rises in WORKPLACES and TRANSIT mobility reflect a reinforcing commuting-and-errand loop: increased workplace attendance raises transit use, which in turn enables more incidental retail stops, producing a compounding increase in RETAIL_REC over the next two weeks that exceeds what either series predicts alone.
candidate_trigger: both WORKPLACES and TRANSIT rise week-on-week simultaneously for two consecutive weeks
evidence_refs: fact:both WORKPLACES and TRANSIT rose in t-2w and t-1w
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC growth rate over the next two weeks is not greater than the growth rate implied by WORKPLACES or TRANSIT alone, or RETAIL_REC declines despite joint increases in both series.

mechanism_narrative: The gradual rise in PARKS mobility, from -61.6 to -56.4, reflects a seasonal pull toward outdoor recreation that substitutes for indoor retail and recreation visits, producing a short-term one-week dip in RETAIL_REC before any rebound.
evidence_refs: fact:PARKS improved from -61.6 to -56.4 over the last four weeks
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC rises over the next week even as PARKS continues to increase, indicating no substitution effect.

mechanism_narrative: RETAIL_REC's week-on-week improvement has stalled, moving from -57.0 to -57.7, after two weeks of rapid recovery, indicating behavioral fatigue or saturation in pent-up demand that will produce a flat-to-negative RETAIL_REC trend over the next week.

evidence_refs: fact:RETAIL_REC moved from -57.0 at t-1w to -57.7 at t-0w
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC resumes a clear upward trend (mean next 28 days > mean last 28 days) despite the recent week-on-week stall.

mechanism_narrative: A widening gap between rising GROCERY_PHARM mobility and stagnant RETAIL_REC signals continued policy restrictions that limit non-essential retail reopening while permitting essential shopping, which will suppress RETAIL_REC growth over the next two weeks.

regime_hint: restrictive policy regime with partial reopening
